name: plan_reachable_linear_contact
summary: Compose linear-contact waypoint generation with generic complete-sequence manipulator selection.

generality.rationale: Object-independent IK composition, but no physical contact feature is modeled; successful press transfer is unvalidated.
assumptions: Straight surface-normal contact is suitable and TCP-origin targeting matches the intended physical contact feature.
Discrete chained IK is only a kinematic endpoint test.
limitations: No finger/pad selection, aperture-dependent contact geometry, gripper/fixed-chassis or continuous collision certification, force control, execution, or effect verification.
Self checking covers non-adjacent active links; other arms are stationary snapshots. Missing scene context leaves clearance unknown; unseen space remains unknown.
Use other waypoint builders for grasping and placing.
tested_tasks: robotwin/press-stapler-aloha-agilex (behavior refactored after harness_v2 iter_005; runtime regression pending)

level.rationale: Composes a task-specific geometry builder with generic physical-pair ranking, TCP transforms, and complete chained IK.

composition.strategy: Build four linear-contact TCP variants, solve each complete sequence across base-ranked arm-effector pairs, optionally reject sampled arm/environment overlaps, and expose explicit IK and collision evidence.

provenance.failure_gap: The prior wrapper mixed contact-specific geometry with generic arm selection, making left/right-arm reasoning unavailable to grasp and place tools.
evidence: The 0.1.x implementation directly generated contact yaw candidates and called a contact-specific IK planner inside the same candidate loop.
